title: Lisa Ling Signs With CAA
description: Lisa Ling, the journalist, producer and author who has logged stints at Channel One, ABC, CNN and CBS News, has tapped CAA to represent her in a va
body:
Lisa Ling, the journalist, producer and author who has logged stints at Channel One, ABC, CNN and CBS News, has tapped CAA to represent her in a variety of fields.

	Ling, who recently worked as a contributor at CBS News, is known for her work hosting documentary-journalism programs ranging from National Geographic’s “Explorer” to CNN’s “This Is Life.” She also spent time as one of the co-hosts at ABC’s daytime show “The View,” and hosted and executive-produced “Our America” for the Oprah Winfrey Network, now part of Skydance. 
	

	Ling has worked as a journalist from a young age, starting first as a teenager for “Scratch,” a nationally syndicated TV program aimed at teens, and then for Channel One, a video-news report aimed at schoolchildren. She traveled abroad and covered war outbreaks in different parts of the world. She previously had a production deal with HBO that resulted in series such as “Take Out,” a look at the world of Asian-American cuisine.

	Her books include titles such as “Mother, Sister, Daughter, Bride: Rituals of Womanhood,” and “Somewhere Inside: One Sister’s Captivity in North Korea and Other’s Fights to Bring Her Home,” about her sister, Laura, who was detained in North Korea after attempting to film refugees along the country’s border with China.

	Ling is founder of MightyLings, a digital platform that promotes intergenerational strength, wellness and spirit building. She serves on the boards of the prison reentry organization CROP, the California Partners Project, The Asian American Foundation and the Kids Mental Health Foundation.

title: Harry Styles Waltzes His Way Through ‘Coming Up Roses’ Music Video
description: Harry Styles puts his waltzing skills to the test in the video for “Coming Up Roses,” the latest single to get the music video treatment from his f
body:
Harry Styles puts his waltzing skills to the test in the video for “Coming Up Roses,” the latest single to get the music video treatment from his fourth album “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally.”

	For the clip, Styles reunites with directing duo Bradley & Pablo, who helmed the videos for “Watermelon Sugar” and “Late Night Talking.” Throughout the visuals, he waltzes with various partners before a woman does an interpretive dance to the song. In the end, they all come together for a photo finish, smiling for the camera.
	



	Styles initially hinted at the release of the music video during the 27th of 30 shows at New York City’s Madison Square Garden on Saturday night. The singer is currently on his “Together, Together” tour, which will conclude its MSG residency on October 31. He’ll wrap up this leg of the trek in Melbourne and Sydney in November and December before picking back up in Glendale, Arizona in April.

	Following his Arizona shows, Styles will perform a series of shows in respective cities including Arlington, Pasadena, Toronto, Chicago, Berlin, Nanterre, Madrid, Rome and Dublin. He’ll bring this live era to a close with three shows at London’s Wembley Stadium on August 24, 27 and 28.

	Variety recently broke the news that famed documentary director John Wilson has been rolling cameras on Styles at MSG since August, capturing footage for a doc expected to blend live performances with a glimpse into Styles’ world. One source described it as featuring authentic human stories of everyone involved in the tour, from the singer and his fans to the countless others behind the scenes.
	

	Styles most recently released his fourth album “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally” this past March. The project, led by the single “Aperture,” debuted at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with 430,000 equivalent album units.

schema.headline: Harry Styles Waltzes His Way Through ‘Coming Up Roses’ Music Video

title: Music Industry Moves: Mary J. Blige Sells Music Catalogs to Primary Wave; Stella Lefty Signs With Make Wake for Management; Boyz II Men Ink With Warner Records Nashville
description: Mary J. Blige has sold undisclosed shares of her publishing and recorded-music assets to Primary Wave Music, the company announced on Monday mornin
body:
Mary J. Blige has sold undisclosed shares of her publishing and recorded-music assets to Primary Wave Music, the company announced on Monday morning. Included in the deal are some of Blige’s greatest hits, including “Family Affair,’ “My Life,” “Mary Jane (All Night Long),” “You Bring Me Joy,” “Be Without You,” “I Can Love You,” and others; further details were not announced. 

	Known universally as “the Queen of Hip-Hop Soul,” over the course of her three-decade-plus career Blige has sold an estimated 50 million records worldwide across 15 studio albums, two live albums and 83 singles, which have garnered her nine Grammy Awards amid 37 Grammy nominations, two Oscar and one Emmy nom. She was honored with a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 2018 and inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2024. She kicked off her first-ever Las Vegas residency, “Mary J. Blige: My Life, My Story.” The 20-date residency began this past May and will run through February 2027 at Dolby Live at Park MGM.
	

	Natalia Nastaskin, Primary Wave’s Chief Content Officer, said “From the moment I heard ‘You Remind Me’ on NY’s KISS-FM, I became a Day 1 Mary J. Blige fan. For over 30 years, she has gifted the world with hit after undeniable hit and in the process has created the soundtrack of our lives. To partner with the Queen herself on her extraordinary catalog and her everlasting legacy is an honor for me and for our entire Primary Wave team.”

	* Sandlot-Atlantic Outpost recording artist Stella Lefty, who is enjoying one of the biggest hits of the year with “Boston,” has signed with Nashville-based Make Wake Artists for management representation. At the company, which also manages Luke Combs, Lefty will be managed by founder and CNO (Chief Navigation Officer) Chris Kappy and managing partner Sophia Sansone.
	

	Launched in 2015, the company’s roster includes Jon Bellion, Flatland Cavalry, and Dylan Marlowe, among others.

	“Stella’s connection to her fans reminds me of Luke’s fan connection very early on… It is real!!!,” Kappy said in a statement. “Stella has the talent, authenticity and drive to build something truly special, and our team is committed to helping her realize that potential.”

	+ Veteran vocal group Boyz II Men have signed with Warner Records Nashville and will launch an all-new country project, scheduled for release in 2027. Since emerging from Philadelphia with their 1991 debut, “Cooleyhighharmony,” the group has sold an estimated 60 million albums worldwide and wont four Grammy Awards and a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

	“Boyz II Men’s global influence is decades in the making,” shared Warner Records Nashville Chair & President, Cris Lacy. “Every genre and culture has benefited from their original music, and their impact on artists in the current country landscape, while perhaps surprising to some, is quite profound. When I learned that growing up listening to artists like Randy Travis was seminal in their desire to collaborate with Nashville’s award-winning singers and songwriters, I knew we had to be a part of it.”

	+ Pop vet JoJo has partnered with Seeker Music, which has acquired the singer-songwriter’s original and re-recorded versions of her first two albums – “JoJo” and “The High Road” – as well as future releases and projects. The celebration kicks off with Seeker’s release of a deluxe 20th anniversary edition of “The High Road,” featuring the original album and four bonus tracks from the original 2006 editions, as well as acoustic versions. Jojo has also collaborated in the past with Seeker CEO and founder Evan Bogart; Seeker already held interest in two of her hits via deals with other cowriters.

	“Deciding who to trust with such a personal and important part of my catalog wasn’t something I took lightly,” Jojo said. “Over time it was heartening to learn more about Seeker’s ethos and see how involved and passionate Evan is — someone who truly understands artists because he is a creator himself. It feels full-circle to have both versions of these albums together with a team committed to finding new ways to amplify it.”
	

	Bogart added, “I’ve personally been such a fan for so long, and it means the world to all of us at Seeker to be partnering with her. This is just the beginning!”

	+ Believe has named Mel Curley as Global Head of Editorial & Marketing Partnerships. Based in New York, Mel will report to Darya Pourshasb, Believe’s Chief Marketing Officer. According to the announcement, Curley will lead Believe’s global EMP strategy, strengthening relationships with key digital platforms and unlocking new editorial and promotional opportunities to support artists and labels growth and international development across Believe’s Artist Services, Label & Artist Solutions and TuneCore.

	She joins from Amazon Music, where she served as Global Head of Independent Label Relations, overseeing relationships with more than 350 independent distributors, labels and artists. Previously, she held senior positions at Arista Records and at Sony Music Entertainment.

	Pourshasb said, “As competition for audience attention intensifies, our ability to connect artists and labels with fans across digital platforms has never been more important, which is why Editorial and Marketing Partnerships are a key pillar of our music marketing strategy. Mel brings an exceptional combination of DSP expertise, music industry experience and strategic vision.”

	+ Hybe Americas has announced the launch of Tru Records, a new record label “created to discover and develop the next generation of Latin pop artists,” according to the announcement. Latin music veteran Alejandro Mejía will be the company’s first general manager, and its first artist is Santos Bravos, the first Latin pop group created by Hybe Americas.

	“The launch of Tru Records represents a unique opportunity to champion Latin American talent and bring it to new audiences around the world,” Mejía said. “Starting this new chapter with Santos Bravos and with the support of Hybe Americas allows us to build careers with international reach while staying true to our Latin identity and the stories we tell.”

schema.headline: Music Industry Moves: Mary J. Blige Sells Music Catalogs to Primary Wave; Stella Lefty Signs With Make Wake for Management; Boyz II Men Ink With Warner Records Nashville

title: Skydance Is Offering Employees Voluntary Buyouts Ahead of Layoffs, Adopts 5-Days-per-Week In-Office Policy
description: Skydance, as it embarks on the work to integrate the businesses of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, is offering certain employees a voluntary
body:
Skydance, as it embarks on the work to integrate the businesses of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, is offering certain employees a voluntary buyout in a “one-time offer.”

	The new program was outlined by chairman and CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz in a memo to staffers Monday.

	“As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that. To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program,” the execs wrote. “Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer.”
	

	They added, “Please know we don’t take any of this lightly. We are clear about what we’re building: a company that tells the stories people around the world love, embraces new ways to connect with audiences, and leads the next era of media and entertainment. We have the talent, the creative firepower and the ambition to do it, and we will get there together.”

	Paramount’s massive $111 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery closed on Oct. 6. In their “Day One” memo to employees that day, Ellison and Kreiz (who was the CEO of Mattel before joining the new Skydance earlier this month) acknowledged that layoffs will be part of the process. “Integrating two companies will bring change, including difficult decisions that affect our workforce,” the execs wrote in that memo. “We are committed to handling this process thoughtfully and respectfully.”
	

	In the Oct. 26 memo, Ellison and Kreiz also said the new Skydance is moving to a mandatory five-days-per-week in-office policy across the company. “We believe in-person collaboration is vital to our culture and to the success of our business. Especially in a creative company like ours, the best ideas come from people in the same room, sharing perspectives, challenging one another and solving problems,” the execs said.  “We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people. We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.”

	Skydance execs have said they are shooting to achieve more than $6 billion in cost savings on an annualized basis within three years, and part of that will come from layoffs. The company has not revealed at this point the extent of the job cuts it expects. According to a report issued by Los Angeles County in August, the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger could result in the loss of some 4,500 film and TV jobs over three years in L.A. alone.

	Read the full memo sent by Skydance’s top brass Monday, a copy of which was obtained by Variety:

	Team,

	At Skydance, our goal is to build the next-generation media and entertainment company, powered by creativity and technology. We are creative-first, audience focused, tech-forward and globally scaled. And in a world of endless choice and fierce competition for attention, we don’t just want to succeed. We want to win.

	To do that, we must be a strong, connected and agile company. Among our business and creative priorities, none matters more than building a strong culture, because it’s the foundation of everything we want to achieve. Winning requires us to work as one team: one company, fully aligned. That means communicating openly and collaborating efficiently across every part of the organization.

	In-Person Collaboration

	We believe in-person collaboration is vital to our culture and to the success of our business. Especially in a creative company like ours, the best ideas come from people in the same room, sharing perspectives, challenging one another and solving problems. Being together isn’t just about showing up. It’s about inspiring one another, learning and coaching, forming friendships and having the casual conversations that spark something great.
	

	With that in mind, we will adopt a five-day in-office policy across all of Skydance. We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people. We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.

	While many of you are already in the office five days a week, we understand this may be a significant change to the daily routines of others. To give you time to plan and adjust, we will take a phased approach by location. You will receive ample notice before changes take effect, and we will work closely with managers to support you through the transition.

	Voluntary Buyout Program

	As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that. To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer.

	We recognize this is a significant decision, and we want you to feel informed and supported. If this applies to you, please review your materials carefully and reach out to your leadership or HR representative with any questions. FAQs and other resources are available on the Skydance Integration Hub, and HR support is also available through My Paramount (legacy Paramount employees) or Ask Employee Connection on WBD One (legacy Warner Bros. employees).

	Please know we don’t take any of this lightly. We are clear about what we’re building: a company that tells the stories people around the world love, embraces new ways to connect with audiences, and leads the next era of media and entertainment. We have the talent, the creative firepower and the ambition to do it, and we will get there together.

	Thank you for your commitment, and for the creativity and passion you bring to your work every day.

	Best,

	David and Ynon

schema.headline: Skydance Is Offering Employees Voluntary Buyouts Ahead of Layoffs, Adopts 5-Days-per-Week In-Office Policy

title: Sharjah Film Festival Partners With UAE’s Media Authority in Push to Assist Emerging Filmmakers
description: The Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth is adding a federal partner to its push to build a more substantial and sustainable pipeline
body:
The Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth is adding a federal partner to its push to build a more substantial and sustainable pipeline for emerging filmmakers. The organization behind the festival signed an agreement with the UAE’s recently established National Media Authority covering areas from film screening procedures to training and technical support.

	The memorandum of understanding was signed Monday on the opening day of SIFF’s 13th edition by the National Media Authority and FANN – Media Discovery Platform, the Sharjah organization that runs the festival and whose name derives from the Arabic word for “art.” The agreement makes the authority an official supporting partner of SIFF while establishing broader cooperation between the two organizations.
	

	The partnership comes as SIFF increasingly looks beyond screenings and workshops to the practical hurdles facing young filmmakers trying to enter the industry. Ahead of the festival, SIFF director Sheikha Jawaher bint Abdullah Al Qasimi told Variety that learning to make a film represents only one part of that journey.

	“Our agreement with the National Media Authority reflects this commitment,” Al Qasimi said Monday. “It is an important step in bringing together national efforts to support the film industry and help emerging filmmakers turn their ideas and perspectives into creative work.”

	The new agreement addresses another piece of that infrastructure. The National Media Authority will help facilitate permits required to screen participating films, coordinating, where necessary, with embassies, consulates, cultural organizations and government entities. Festival teams will also receive training on the authority’s electronic services and technical support intended to streamline regulatory procedures.
	

	The agreement comes during a period of restructuring for the UAE’s media landscape. Established by federal decree in December 2025, the National Media Authority took over functions previously held by the UAE Media Council, National Media Office and Emirates News Agency, bringing media regulation and development under a single federal body. Its mandate includes media policy and legislation, licensing and content standards.

	“Supporting content created for children and youth is an important part of our strategy to develop a competitive and sustainable national media sector,” National Media Authority secretary-general Mohammed Saeed Al Shehhi said Monday.

	For FANN, the agreement adds a federal institution to an ecosystem Al Qasimi has argued must extend beyond the festival itself. SIFF’s expanding Industry Hub and pitching program are designed to connect filmmakers with producers, supporters and funders, with the aim of turning introductions into financing, production support and longer-term collaborations.

	The agreement also allows National Media Authority representatives to participate in festival juries and film evaluations, while the two organizations will collaborate on SIFF’s media and communications activities.

	SIFF runs through Nov. 1, with 71 films from 38 countries in its selection.

schema.headline: Sharjah Film Festival Partners With UAE’s Media Authority in Push to Assist Emerging Filmmakers

title: Walter Koenig, Chekov on Original ‘Star Trek,’ Dies at 90
description: Walter Koenig, who memorably played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series and seven “Star Trek” feature films, died Sunday in Los Angeles, Vari
body:
Walter Koenig, who memorably played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series and seven “Star Trek” feature films, died Sunday in Los Angeles, Variety has confirmed. He was 90. 

	His reps said in a statement, “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world. He passed of old age at home in North Hollywood last night surrounded by his daughter and niece. 
	

	“Best known for his iconic role as Pavel Chekov in ‘Star Trek: The Original Series,’ Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit. Beyond ‘Star Trek,’ his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft. His remarkable talent continued to shine in his later years, most recently with his performance in the short film ‘Mr. Fleischmann,’ for which he received the Platinum Award for Best Actor at the 2026 Independent Shorts Awards — a fitting recognition of a lifetime devoted to his craft.

	“Walter’s legacy extends far beyond the screen. Through countless convention appearances and interactions with fans, he shared his kindness, wit, and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him. He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it.

	“On behalf of all of us, we extend our deepest condolences to Walter’s family, friends, colleagues, and the millions of fans whose lives he touched over the decades.

	“Thank you, Walter, for the memories, the inspiration, and for boldly going where few have gone before.”
	

	Koenig’s Chekov, an arrogant young navigation officer in the original series, was introduced to the series to appeal to teenage viewers — his hairstyle recalled that of the Monkees’ Davy Jones.

	The Russian-born Chekov was also used to poke fun at the Soviet way of falsely taking credit for every important human invention.

	Koenig played Chekov in the 2015 TV movie “Star Trek: Renegades,” set at a time in which the character has been elevated to admiral. The film, aimed as a backdoor pilot for a new “Star Trek” television series, was funded through crowdsourcing. 

	The Chekov character was not included in “Star Trek: The Animated Series” in the early ’70s because of the show’s limited budget, but Koenig penned an episode of the series entitled “The Infinite Vulcan.”

	Koenig’s Chekov was central to the plot of 1982’s “Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan” and consequently the actor enjoyed considerable screen time in the film, generally considered the best of the “Star Trek” movies.

	Koenig was also associated with another sci-fi franchise, J. Michael Straczynski’s “Babylon 5,” in which he played the evil Psi Cop Alfred Bester (named by the show’s creators after the science fiction writer). He appeared in 12 episodes of that show from 1994-98.

	Walter Marvin Koenig was born in Chicago. The family of Russian Jewish heritage was originally named Koenigsberg, and he attended Fieldston High School in Fieldston, N.Y., where he did some stage work, before starting at Grinnell College in Iowa, where he was initially pre-med; he transferred to and graduated from UCLA with a degree in psychology. After a professor urged him to pursue a career in acting, he began studying at the Neighborhood Playhouse in New York; there his classmates included Christopher Lloyd, with whom he would be reunited on “Star Trek III: The Search for Spock,” in which Lloyd played the villainous Klingon Commander Kruge, as well as James Caan and Dabney Coleman.

	Koenig made his small-screen debut with an uncredited role in an episode of “Combat!” in 1962, followed by guest-starring roles on “The Untouchables,” “General Hospital,” “The Alfred Hitchcock Hour,” “Ben Casey,” “Gidget” and “I Spy.” After the original “Star Trek” series went off the air in 1969, he worked occasionally in TV,  guesting on “The Virginian,” “Ironside” and “Columbo” (in an episode that had William Shatner as the special guest star). He played a deputy sheriff in an unremarkable low-budget film called “Nightmare Honeymoon,” starring Dack Rambo.
	

	During the 1980s, when he was busy with the “Star Trek” movies, he appeared as Pompey in a 1984 TV adaptation of “Antony & Cleopatra” that also featured Nichelle Nichols and future “Star Trek: Enterprise” actor James Avery.

	The actor appeared in a string of low-budget science fiction movies over the years, including “Moontrap,” in which he starred, and “Deadly Weapon,” both in 1989; as well as Cynthia Rothrock martial arts vehicle “Sworn to Justice” in 1996 and independent horror film “Mad Cowgirl” in 2006.

	A one-character film that Koenig wrote and performed, “You’re Never Alone When You’re a Schizophrenic,” was screened at the 1996 New York Film Festival.

	He voiced Chekov in a variety of “Star Trek” video games, including 1998’s “Starfleet Academy: Chekov’s Lost Missions.”

	The actor guested on an episode of the CBS sitcom “Almost Perfect” titled “Where No Woman Has Gone Before” in 1997 and voiced himself on a 2002 episode of “Futurama” titled “Where No Fan Has Gone Before,” which also featured the voices of William Shatner and Leonard Nimoy, among other “Star Trek” regulars. He also guested on “Diagnosis Murder” (in an episode that featured several other “Star Trek” actors) and “Son of the Beach.”

	He penned the 2008 sci-fi legal thriller “InAlienable,” in which he also appeared (the tagline was “From the mind of Walter Koenig”).

	Koenig also had a stage career that spanned three decades.

	In the early 1990s he toured with Mark Lenard (who played Spock’s father Sarek on “Star Trek”) in “The Boys in Autumn,” in which Koenig played a middle-aged Tom Sawyer reunited after decades apart with Lenard’s Huckleberry Finn.

	Koenig also directed theater, including “Hotel Parsadiso” for Company of Angels, “Becket” for Theatre 40, “America Hurrah!” at Oxford Theater, “Twelve Angry Men” at the Rita Hayworth Theatre, “Matrix” at the Gascon Theatre Institute and “Three by Ten” at Actors Alley in Los Angeles.

	Koenig taught acting classes at UCLA, at Actors Alley and elsewhere.

	His satiric fantasy novel “Buck Alice and the Actor-Robot” was re-released in 2006; he created the comic book “Raver” published by Malibu Comics. In 2013 Bluewater Comics published the graphic novel “Walter Koenig’s Things to Come.”
	

	Koenig penned the memoirs “Chekov’s Enterprise: A Personal Journal of the Making of Star Trek — The Motion Picture,” published in 1980, and “Warped Factors — A Neurotic’s Guide to the Universe,” published in 1998.

	Anton Yelchin portrayed a much younger Chekov in the rebooted “Star Trek” films.

	Back in the days of the original “Star Trek” series there was a period of tension between Koenig and George Takei, who played Sulu, but the two came to be close friends, and in September 2008, Koenig served as best man at Takei’s wedding to Brad Altman.

	Koenig a daughter, actress-writer Danielle Koenig. A son, actor and editor Andrew Koenig, died in 2010.

schema.headline: Walter Koenig, Chekov on Original ‘Star Trek,’ Dies at 90

title: Instagram Is Testing Ability to Share Videos up to 90 Minutes Long and Launches on Apple TV — but Unlike YouTube, It’s Still Not Going to Pay Creators
description: Meta‘s Instagram is trying to make itself a better place for watching and sharing longer-form entertainment content from digital creators, includin
body:
Meta‘s Instagram is trying to make itself a better place for watching and sharing longer-form entertainment content from digital creators, including testing out video lengths of up to 90 minutes and letting users watch Reels and more on Apple TV.

	The moves are meant to position Instagram as a bigger potential competitor to YouTube. But for now, Instagram is still not planning a revenue-sharing program akin to YouTube’s that would compensate creators for sharing their work on the platform.
	

	Instagram announced the test of the new features in (of course) a video shared Monday on the platform.

	“Instagram is all about connecting people over creativity. And creativity is so much more than just short-form video or posting carousels,” Instagram VP of product Tessa Lyons said in the video, alongside Instagram head Adam Mosseri. Lyons said Instagram wants to accommodate creators who are telling stories in different ways on the platform, such as in episodic series, and that it’s seeing some sharing clips from long-form videos to drive discovery of that content.

	Mosseri noted, “I have been against doing long-form video on the platform for a long time.” One of his concerns historically has been “how do we make sure that we keep Instagram not just about entertainment, but also about connecting with friends.” 

	“If you watch a video [on Instagram] for 10 or 20 or 30 minutes, it’s a lot of Reels, photos and carousels that you might not have sent to a friend,” which means fewer likes and shares, he said. But now, Mosseri has been sold on the need for Instagram to “lean into” long-form videos, including on TVs.
	

	The new Instagram Features (which it is testing in the U.S. with a small group of creators) allows longer horizontal videos to Instagram, in some cases up to 90 minutes long. Creators can also share clips as Reels to help people discover a long-form feature video. And soon, Instagram Lives will show up beyond just a creator’s followers, to be discovered by audiences in the Reels tab. Instagram also is planning to introduce a new feature that will let you use your phone as a remote control for playback of videos on TVs.

	“Creators can build a fuller body of work on Instagram, while fans have more ways to discover and keep up with what they love,” an Instagram rep said.

	As for whether Instagram will introduce an ad-revenue share in the future, the Instagram spokesperson said “it’s too early to share a long-term monetization model, but we’re exploring ways for creators to earn from brands, fans and Instagram, including performance-based incentives. Over time, we think there will be compounding benefits for creators to tell new stories, reach new audiences, and find new partners, which should lead to many monetization opportunities.”

	Here’s a rundown of Instagram’s new features:

title: Montclair Film Festival 2026 Reveals Full Winners List: ‘Possible Love,’ ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Take Top Honors (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
The Montclair Film Festival has crowned some of the year’s best films.

	Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love” earned top honors in the festival’s ficti
body:
The Montclair Film Festival has crowned some of the year’s best films.

	Lee Chang-dong’s “Possible Love” earned top honors in the festival’s fiction feature competition, while Pegah Ahangarani’s “Rehearsals for a Revolution” was named the winner of the Bruce Sinofsky Award in the documentary feature competition. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes’ documentary “One in a Million” was awarded the special jury prize.


	Stephanie Ahn’s “Bedford Park” and William D. Caballero’s “TheyDream” were co-winners of the Future/Now competition and the $5,000 Mark Urman award for filmmaking.
	

	Audience award winners included Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine” for fiction feature, Juliane Dressner and Miriam Shor’s “My NDA” for documentary feature, Ryûsuke Hamaguchi’s “All of a Sudden” for best of world cinema, and Steven Leckart’s “An Unknown Substance” took honors for best short film.

	Among the winners in the shorts competitions were K. Xian Ming Yu’s “I See You in the Flood,” MarsVerrone’s “Buckskin” and Jeannette Louie’s “Us Being Epic.”

	Additionally, Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson’s “Mouse” was awarded the Junior Jury prize, with a special jury prize for excellence in cinematography given to Senzo Ueno for his work on Hirokazu Kore-eda’s “Look Back.”

	“Congratulations to our award winners for their outstanding work,” Montclair Film artistic director Tom Hall said in a statement. “We are incredibly grateful to all of the artists who shared their films with our audiences at this year’s festival. The connection these films forged with our festival audiences created an incredible atmosphere of conversation, connection and community. We are so honored to have been given the opportunity to bring these films to our screens, and look forward to continuing our support of these films in our cinemas and in our community throughout the coming year.”

schema.headline: Montclair Film Festival 2026 Reveals Full Winners List: ‘Possible Love,’ ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Take Top Honors (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Bill Nighy Joins Caitriona Balfe in Alfonso Cuaron Series ‘Ascension’ at Apple TV
description:

	Nighy will star i
body:
Bill Nighy has joined the cast of Alfonso Cuarón upcoming horror thriller series “Ascension” at Apple TV, Variety has learned. 

	Nighy will star in the show alongside previously announced lead Caitríona Balfe. It was originally announced with a series pickup at Apple in August and is inspired by the novel “Last Days” by Adam Nevill. 

	The logline for the series states that it follows Rose (Balfe), “a relentless documentary filmmaker and recently divorced mother, brilliant at uncovering others’ truths but struggling to resolve her own. When Rose begins a project on a mysterious 20th-century cult known as the Church of Ascension, she finds unexpected refuge in its teachings – until she discovers something far more insidious beneath.”
	

	Exact details on Nighy’s role are being kept under wraps.

	This is the latest recent casting announcement for Nighy, as it was previously reported he would guest star in “Star Trek: Starfleet Academy” Season 2 at Paramount+. His other recent TV credits include “Ride or Die” and “Lazarus” at Amazon and “The Man Who Fell to Earth” at Showtime (now Paramount+). In film, Nighy received an Oscar, BAFTA, and Golden Globe nomination for his work in 2023’s “Living.” He is also known for his work in the “Pirates of the Carribean” franchise, “Shaun of the Dead,” “Notes on a Scandal,” and “Love Actually.” 

	He is repped by Independent Talent in the U.K., UTA and Public Eye Communications. 

	Alfonso Cuarón is co-writer on the series along with his brother Carlos Cuarón as well as Natalie Erika James (“Apartment 7A,” “Relic”) and Christian White (“Apartment 7A,” “Relic”), with all four executive producing. James and White also serve as co-showrunners, with James serving as lead director. Balfe will executive produce in addition to starring. Alfonso executive produces under his Esperanto Filmoj banner, which has an overall TV deal with Apple.
	

	Esperanto Filmoj’s Gabriela Rodriguez and Richard Schwartz will executive produce. Steve Golin, David Levine and Zack Hayden executive produce for Anonymous Content. Anonymous will produce the show, with Apple Studios serving as the studio.

schema.headline: Bill Nighy Joins Caitriona Balfe in Alfonso Cuaron Series ‘Ascension’ at Apple TV

title: ‘Baywatch’ Reboot Sets January Premiere Date on Fox
description:
“Baywatch” is bringing sunshine to the winter, as Fox’s reboot of the blockbuster beach series will premiere on Jan. 6 at 9 p.m.

	The continuation
body:
“Baywatch” is bringing sunshine to the winter, as Fox’s reboot of the blockbuster beach series will premiere on Jan. 6 at 9 p.m.

	The continuation of the 1990s sensation stars Stephen Amell as a grown-up version of Hobie Buchannon, the wild child from the original series. The show follows Hobie, now a Baywatch Captain, following in the footsteps of his father, Mitch, while his world is turned upside down by the surprise arrival of Charlie (Jessica Belkin), the daughter he never knew. Eager to carry on the family legacy, Charlie strives to become a Baywatch lifeguard alongside her dad.
	

	Shay Mitchell, Brooks Nader, Hassie Harrison, Livvy Dunne, Noah Beck, David Chokachi and Thaddeus LaGrone star alongside Amell and Belkin. Ashley Moore, Luke Eisner, Nadia Gray, Kylar Miranda, and Charlie McElveen appear in recurring cast roles, and hip-hop star Megan Thee Stallion also makes an appearance.

	The “Baywatch” reboot was picked up for the 2026-2027 broadcast season by Fox back in September 2025 with a 12-episode order. The series held an open casting call in early 2026 and began production in Los Angeles in the spring.

	The original “Baywatch” series debuted in 1989 and was, at its peak, the most-watched show in the world, airing in over 200 countries. The ensemble cast included David Hasselhoff as head lifeguard Mitch Buchannon and helped launch the acting careers of stars like Pamela Anderson and Carmen Electra. The show also spawned the spinoff “Baywatch Nights” and, in 2017, was rebooted as a failed feature film starring Dwayne Johnson and Zac Efron.
	

	The reboot is executive produced by showrunner Matt Nix alongside McG, Michael Berk, Greg Bonann, Doug Schwartz, Dante Di Loreto and Mike Horowitz. McG also directed the premiere episode. The series is co-produced by Fox Entertainment and Fremantle.

	Watch a new promo for the series below.

title: 'Star Trek' Actor Walter Koenig Dead at 90
description:
Actor Walter Koenig
                          Dead at 90 ...
                          Played Chekov i
body:
Actor Walter Koenig
                          Dead at 90 ...
                          Played Chekov in Original 'Star Trek' Series
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 26, 2026
                            9:27 AM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
            Walter Koenig -- the TV star best known for playing Ensign Pavel Chekov in the original "Star Trek" series -- has died ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            The late actor's rep tells us ... Walter's daughter, Danielle, and his niece were by his side when he died of old age at his home in North Hollywood on Sunday.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The rep noted his enormous talent -- including his recent win at the 2026 Independent Shorts Awards for his performance in the film "Mr. Fleischmann" -- as well as his larger legacy.
      

            At conventions, the rep says Walter "shared his kindness, wit, and appreciation with everyone fortunate enough to meet him. He understood what Star Trek meant to people and embraced the community that grew around it."
      
    
            The rep expressed condolences to Walter's loved ones and fans ... before adding, "Thank you, Walter, for the memories, the inspiration, and for boldly going where few have gone before."
      
    
            Walter began acting onscreen in the early 1960s, appearing in bit roles on shows like "Gidget" and "I Spy" before landing the role of Chekov, which he played on 36 episodes of "Star Trek."
      
    
            He later reprised his role in "Star Trek: The Motion Picture," "Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan," "Star Trek III: The Search for Spock" and several other sequels.
      
    
            Walter's credits also include "Babylon 5," "Columbo," and "Futurama" ... among many others.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            He was predeceased by his son, Andrew Koenig, who died by suicide in 2010.
      
    
        
                    
                      JUNE 2009
                  
      
    
            We last caught up with Walter in 2009 ... when we asked him about the secret to a successful marriage. He and his wife Judy were married for nearly 60 years ... until she passed in 2022.
      
    
            He was 90.
      
    
            RIP

schema.headline: 'Star Trek' Actor Walter Koenig Dead at 90

title: Brooke Hogan Rips Sale of Hulk Hogan's Mansion, Calls Out 'Dirty Money'
description:
Brooke Hogan
                          My Dad's Mansion Sold for Dirty Money!!!
body:
Brooke Hogan
                          My Dad's Mansion Sold for Dirty Money!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 26, 2026
                            8:19 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  October 26, 2026
                                9:56 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Brooke Hogan has two words for the people she believes benefited from the sale of her late father Hulk Hogan's Florida mansion ... "dirty money."
      
    
            Hulk's daughter unloaded on Instagram after the Clearwater property sold ... mourning the loss of a home she says was supposed to be where her dad and now-ex-wife, Jennifer McDaniel, grew old together.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            She shared a photo of the mansion with a "SOLD" sticker slapped across it ... recalling the countless memories she made there with her father.
      

            Brooke also posted a more pointed message alongside another photo of the property ... "You took my dad."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            She recalled cooking with Hulk, watching "Jerry Springer," playing music and crying together ... even remembering how she'd sit beside him for hours in his chair where he later died.
      
    
            But Brooke's anger goes well beyond the real estate deal ... claiming her father's entire world changed after she was no longer part of his life.
      
    
            She wrote ... "And now it's all gone. Sold for profit. Just like him...used for f***ing everyone else's gain. Saddest ending I've ever seen."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Brooke also shared another pointed message ... reminding people she was there for the 15 years before the "vultures swooped in conveniently," saying she loved, cherished and cared for her father while keeping track of his medications.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Hulk's Florida mansion sold for $5.9 million, well below its original nearly $11 million asking price. A neighboring guest cottage also sold for $2.8 million.
      
    
            Hulk died in July 2025 at age 71 after suffering a medical emergency at the Clearwater property.

title: Backstreet Boys' AJ McLean Reveals How Drake's 40th Birthday Show Came Together
description:
Backstreet Boys' AJ McLean
                          How We Made Drake's Birthday Wish Come True
body:
Backstreet Boys' AJ McLean
                          How We Made Drake's Birthday Wish Come True
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              October 26, 2026
                            8:15 AM PDT
                                                                            
              
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Drake had two dream acts in mind for his 40th birthday bash ... and lucky for him, the Backstreet Boys were available to make his wish come true.
      
    
            AJ McLean is spilling the beans on how the boy band's surprise performance at the rapper's lavish New York City party came together ... revealing Drake's manager reached out with a pretty specific request.
      
    
      
      AJ McLean of the Backstreet Boys reveals how their surprise performance at Drake’s birthday celebration came together.
“His manager hit us up and said Drake only wanted two things for his birthday. Sade to perform or the Backstreet Boys.” https://t.co/i10dpgh0UU
              @NightOwlsHQx
          
  
    
            AJ says Drake only wanted one of two acts to perform at his birthday celebration ... either Sade or the Backstreet Boys.
      

            The group still had to get everyone on board ... and AJ admits he was a little unsure about Kevin Richardson, who usually switches into full-on football dad mode when the band isn't working.
      
    
            But AJ had a feeling Kevin would say yes ... joking his two sons, who are huge Drake fans, would've been furious if their dad passed up the opportunity.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            And it sounds like Kevin made the most of the gig ... with AJ joking he was practically glued to Drake the entire night.
      
    
            "Anytime Drake moved anywhere, Kevin was right there," AJ said, laughing about his bandmate's newfound friendship with the birthday boy.
      
    
            As TMZ previously reported ... Drake was absolutely beside himself when the Backstreet Boys surprised him at his 40th birthday bash Friday at Cipriani 42nd Street, even joining the group to belt out their hit "I Want It That Way."
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            The party was no ordinary birthday celebration either ... with more than 400 guests, luxury Chanel and Hermès giveaways, and a game offering cash prizes as high as $1 million.
      
    
            Safe to say ... Drake got it his way.

schema.headline: Backstreet Boys' AJ McLean Reveals How Drake's 40th Birthday Show Came Together
